This document describes an application profile, in this case OSLO Mobility - Timetable and Planning: Time Tables (Application Profile). The application profile specifies a semantic data model covering a set of usecases. The specification consists of terms with their constraints (cardinalities, codelists, usage guidelines).

Summary

The OSLO Mobility – Timetable and Planning: Time Tables application profile describes how to use the terms from the corresponding vocabulary to describe the network topology and timetable of a public transport network.

The standard is based on the EPIP profile on NETEX.

Use cases for this standard are: route planning, cartography (network plans), timetable and looking up stops/lines.

Public transport is typically offered in the form of Lines, which can be grouped according to the mode of transport (train, tram, bus, etc.) and are part of a Network. These Lines follow certain Routes in the field, the model allows to describe the direction and geometry of these Routes by means of Waypoints and connections between them, the Route Links.

Another part of the model describes the service offered by De Lijnen: the places where stops are made and the times at which stops are made.

A Line follows a so-called Ride Pattern, i.e. the sequence of Points that are visited by the Line. Its specialization, a Service Pattern, describes the sequence of Points where one actually stops. These are the so-called Planned Stopping Points: places where passengers can board or disembark. These logical stops can be linked to physical stops (class Stop) that are described separately in the application profile OSLO Mobility – Timetable and Planning: Stops.

For each point served by a Line or where passengers stop, Passage Times can be specified. These can be grouped by stop and then form the typical time tables that can be found there. They can also be arranged according to the Journey Pattern of a Line and then describe an individual Service Journey with the Arrival Times at the stops.

A specific Service Ride is not necessarily carried out on a daily basis, it may be limited to certain Day types, e.g. only on weekdays. The model allows to describe these Day Types and link them to actual dates (Operational Days) and periods (Operational Periods) in order to arrive at a complete Service Calendar.

Finally, we mention supporting classes, e.g. to indicate the parties that offer or carry out the transport (respectively the Authority and the Operator) or to describe Vehicle types and their Passenger capacity or a class that supports route planning (Service Trip Connection).

Address

Description
Information that makes it possible to refer in a structured and unique way to a building unit, a berth, a location or a plot on the basis of a municipality name, a street name, a house number and possibly a bus number and a postal code.
Usage
The definition refers to Belgian Addresses. In other countries, an Address may refer to other geographical objects (not a building unit or parcel) or may consist of other designations (different from house number and bus number) or of components other than street name, municipality name or postal code. Foreign addresses can be exchanged using the Address Representation object. More detail on this class in the INSPRE Address specification.
Properties
No properties have been defined for this entity.

Description

Link Sequence

RegisteredOrganization

Description
Organization with a legal status established by registration. Compare with a formal organization where this status can also be obtained in another way.
Usage
In Belgium, like in many other countries, the following kinds Organizations must register: company, sole proprietorship, government body, foundation… Upon registration, the Organization receives a company number and its details are entered in a central registry called Crossrads Bank for Enterprises (CBE). More details on this class in the Registered Organization Vocabulary.
Subclass of
FormalOrganization
Properties
For this entity the following properties are defined: legalName , registration .
Property Expected Range Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
legalName LanguageString 1 Legally registered name of the organization. Possibly in different languages.
registration Identifier 1 Identifier that the organization obtained upon registration. In the CBE this would be the enterprisenumber.

ServiceJourneyLink

Description
The connection between two successive Scheduled Stop Points in a Service Journey. Since a Journey is always valid for a specific time (on a specific Day Type), each Service Journey Link has a specific departure and arrival time. Service Journey Links allow Route Planners to more easily calculate the shortest Routes.

arrivalTime DateTime 1 Time when the Link arrives.
departureStop ScheduledStopPoint 1 Stop Place from where the Link departs.
departureTime DateTime 1 Time when the Link departs.
forAlighting Boolean 1 Indicates if the Link is for alighting.
forBoarding Boolean 1 Indicates if the Link is for boarding.
line Line 1 The Line.

Datatypes

AddressRepresentation

Description
Easier to read of a structured address with only the basic or combined data, intended for the use of an address as an attribute of another object or as a label.
Usage
For example as an attribute of a person or building or as a label on a letter or a map.
Properties
For this datatype the following properties are defined: administrativeUnitName , busNumber , country , fullAddress , houseNumber , locatorDesignator , municipalityName , postcode , postName , postOfficeBox , refersTo , thoroughfare .
Property Expected Range Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
administrativeUnitName LanguageString 1 Name of the adminstrative unit of the Address.
busNumber String 0..1 Officially assigned alphanumeric code that is added to the house number to distinguish several building units, pitches, berths or plots that have the same house number. Specialization of locatorIndicator intended for Belgian addresses.
country LanguageString 0..1 Country in which the address is located.
fullAddress LanguageString 0..1 The complete address in one string, formatted or not.
houseNumber String 0..1 Alphanumeric code officially assigned to building units, berths, stands or plots. Specialization of locatorIndicator intended for Belgian addresses.
locatorDesignator String 0..* A number or string of characters that uniquely identifies the location within the relevant scope. The full identification of the locator could include one or more locator designators. The scope is for example the street for a housenumber or the housenumber for a busnumber.
municipalityName LanguageString 0..1 Municipality name of the address.
postcode String 0..1 Code that identifies the geographical area that groups addresses for postal purposes.
postName LanguageString 0..1 Name indicating the geographical area that groups addresses for postal purposes.
postOfficeBox String 0..1 PO Box number in a post office.
refersTo Address 0..1 Address from which the address representation is derived. This is only possible for Belgian addresses, as Address here means a Belgian Address.
thoroughfare LanguageString 0..1 An address component that represents the name of a passageway or passageway from one location to another. A thoroughfare is not necessarily a road, it might be a waterway or some other feature.

Property Expected Range Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
address AddressRepresentation 0..1 Address that can be written to or visited.
Availability OpeningHoursSpecification 0..1 Period in which contact can be made. For example indication of the season in which contact can be made. Start and end date according to ISO8601 syntax.
Contact name String 0..1 Name of the person you can contact, for example.
email String 0..1 Email address to which one can send an e-mail.
form of address LanguageString 0..1 Title that is used to write to someone or address someone or to refer to someone. For example Mr/Mrs, Excellency, Doctor...
openingHours TypedString 0..1 Hours within which contact can be made. Syntax according to schema.org for opening hours. For example if contact can be made between 8 am and 8 pm Monday to Saturday and between 8 am and 6 pm on Sunday this will be coded as Mon-Sat 8 am-8 pm, Sun 8 am-6 pm.
phone String 0..1 Phone number where one can call.
Website URI 0..1 Website that can be surfed.

Polygon

Description
Surface consisting of 1 outer boundary and 0 or more inner boundaries. Each inner boundary forms a hole in the polygon.
Usage
The boundaries are so-called linear rings, that is, they are closed (non-self-intersecting) LineStrings. The outer boundary is distinguished from the inner boundary by the clockwise and counterclockwise directions in which the ring runs.
Subclass of
Geometry
Properties
No properties have been defined for this datatype.

QuantitativeValue

Description
Indication of the quantity of a certain characteristic of an object.
Usage
For example, the height of an object, the weight, the temperature, etc. It concerns a characteristic that can be expressed numerically and in a certain unit. Qualitative indications such as high, low, etc. are therefore not included.

Property Expected Range Cardinality Description Usage Codelist
StandardUnit StandardUnit 0..1 The standardized unit in which the value is expressed.
Unity String 0..1 The unit in which the value is expressed. To be used if no standard unit is known.
value Number 1 Number that can be used to express the quantity of the characteristic.

StandardUnit

Description
Unit established by a standardizing organization.
Usage
Datatype can be a URI or a TypedString. In the first case, reference is made to units published on the web, preferably those from qudt, for example http://qudt.org/vocab/unit/M for meter. In the case of a TypedString, preference is given to the UCUM codes, for example "km/h"^^http://w3id.org/lindt/custom_datatypes#ucumunit.
Properties
No properties have been defined for this datatype.

Combination of a string and the type of what the string represents.

For example, '20170901' as a string and 'date' as a type. Allows automatic interpretation of the string.

Terminology used (external)

This section provides an overview of how terminology from vocabularies has been used in this model.

This implementation model relies on terms from these self-managed vocabularies:

  • https://data.vlaanderen.be/ns/adres

External terminology, which falls outside the in-house namespace data.vlaanderen.be, is listed in the table below with the label, as found in the model, and the underlying URI.

When reusing external terminology, the principles of the SEMIC Style Guide are applied. This means that one agrees to the underlying definition, labels and restrictions associated with the URI in the context of the implementation model. The definitions, labels and usage notes must therefore not contradict those of the URI.
